Dependency updates with strong defaults.


## Examples

Report updates for the current checkout

```sh
patchula lookup
```

Browse updates and apply selected ones

```sh
patchula tui
```

Exit 3 in CI while updates are waiting

```sh
patchula apply --check
```

Write only GitHub Actions updates

```sh
patchula apply --manager github-actions
```

Run this checkout's repository on its remote server

```sh
patchula remote run
```

Run the GitHub App webhook server

```sh
patchula serve --settings settings.pkl
```

- **Usage:** `patchula [FLAGS] <SUBCOMMAND>`

## Global Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-v --verbose` | Show cache details, request counts, and phase timings; repeat for debug logs. |  |
| `--color <WHEN>` | Control ANSI color in output. One of `auto`, `always`, `never`. | `auto` |
| `--json` | Emit command results and errors as JSON; configs stay Pkl. |  |

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |
| `-V --version` | Print version |  |

## `patchula apply`

- **Usage:** `patchula apply [FLAGS]`

Write available updates into the current working tree, without branches or pull requests.

Exit codes: 0 = nothing selected is left to apply; 1 = runtime error; 2 = usage or configuration error; 3 = selected updates are still waiting (`--check` or `--dry-run` found some, or some could not be written in place); 4 = a dependency's lookup failed, so its updates are unknown. 4 takes precedence over 3.

### Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cache <DIR>` | Cache directory, shared across checkouts (default: `patchula` in the user cache directory: `~/Library/Caches` on macOS, else `XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache`). |  |
| `--settings <FILE>` | Operator settings file; also PATCHULA_SETTINGS (default: `patchula/settings.pkl` in `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config`, when present). |  |
| `--concurrency <N>` | Maximum concurrency (1–100), overriding the settings file; HTTP limits are per host (default: 8). |  |
| `--config <FILE>` | Local Pkl config file to use instead of the working tree's `patchula.pkl`. |  |
| `--default-config` | Use default configuration when the working tree has no `patchula.pkl`, instead of prompting. Conflicts with `--config`. |  |
| `--manager <MANAGER>` | Only updates from this manager; repeat for more. One of `npm`, `bun`, `github-actions`, `mise`, `cargo`, `dockerfile`, `compose`, `go`, `terraform`, `kubernetes`, `kustomize`, `flux`, `helm-values`, `pyproject`, `pre-commit`, `helm`, `devcontainer`, `woodpecker`, `copier`, `maven`, `gradle`, `nuget`, `bundler`, `composer`, `gitlabci`, `gitlabci-include`, `nix`, `apm`, `pkl`, `regex`. |  |
| `--dependency <PATTERN>` | Only dependencies matching this name or package, with config's `glob:`, `regex:` and `!`; repeat for more. |  |
| `--type <TYPE>` | Only updates of this type; repeat for more. One of `major`, `minor`, `patch`, `pin`, `digest`. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Print the unified diff of what would be written, and write nothing. |  |
| `--check` | Write nothing; exit 3 if any selected update is waiting, or 4 if a lookup failed. |  |
| `--copier` | Also run `copier update` for each selected template before other updates. Template code runs locally as you; the tree must be clean and `--trust` is never passed. |  |
| `--copier-defaults` | With `--copier`, take default answers for copier prompts, for use without a terminal. |  |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples

Write every available update

```sh
patchula apply
```

Write nothing; exit 3 if updates are waiting

```sh
patchula apply --check
```

Show patch updates as a unified diff

```sh
patchula apply --dry-run --type patch
```

Write only actions/* updates

```sh
patchula apply --manager github-actions --dependency 'glob:actions/*'
```

## `patchula completion`

- **Usage:** `patchula completion [--install] [--force] <SHELL>`

Print or install shell completion scripts.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<SHELL>` | Shell to generate completions for. One of `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `nu`, `nushell`, `powershell`, `pwsh`, `zsh`. |  |

### Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--install` | Write the script where the shell looks for it instead of printing it |  |
| `--force` | With --install, replace a file that was not generated by usage. The file is overwritten without a backup, which is why this is labeled destructive. |  |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples

Install fish completions

```sh
patchula completion fish --install
```

Print the zsh completion script

```sh
patchula completion zsh
```

## `patchula lookup`

- **Usage:** `patchula lookup [FLAGS] [OWNER/REPO]…`

Report available updates without writing; omit repositories to scan the current working tree.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[OWNER/REPO]…` | Repositories as owner/repo, read through the GitHub API; omit for the current checkout. |  |

### Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all-repos` | Scan every repository the token can reach. |  |
| `--cache <DIR>` | Cache directory, shared across checkouts (default: `patchula` in the user cache directory: `~/Library/Caches` on macOS, else `XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache`). |  |
| `--settings <FILE>` | Operator settings file; also PATCHULA_SETTINGS (default: `patchula/settings.pkl` in `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config`, when present). |  |
| `--concurrency <N>` | Maximum concurrent repository scans (1–100), overriding the settings file; HTTP limits are per host (default: 8). |  |
| `--config <FILE>` | Local Pkl config override applied to every selected repository. |  |
| `--config-dir <DIR>` | Per-repository overrides: `DIR/<owner>/<name>.pkl`, then `DIR/<name>.pkl`; other repositories use their own `patchula.pkl`, or are skipped without one. Conflicts with `--config`. |  |
| `--default-config` | Use default configuration when the working tree has no `patchula.pkl`, instead of prompting. Conflicts with `--config` and `--config-dir`. |  |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples

Report updates for the current checkout

```sh
patchula lookup
```

Read two repositories through the API

```sh
patchula lookup acme/app acme/api
```

Emit the report as JSON

```sh
patchula lookup --json
```

## `patchula remote`

- **Usage:** `patchula remote <SUBCOMMAND>`

Run commands on a Count Patchula server with its credentials and warm caches.

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples


## `patchula run`

- **Usage:** `patchula run [FLAGS] [OWNER/REPO]…`

Create or update dependency branches and pull requests on GitHub with verified API commits.

Reads GitHub rather than the working tree, even with `--dry-run`. With no repository, runs this checkout's GitHub repository; `--dir` with `--dry-run` plans from a local directory instead.

Failed lookups are reported but the run still exits 0, since it keeps the pull requests it could plan; it holds off auto-merge and closing pull requests for that repository.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[OWNER/REPO]…` | Repositories as owner/repo, read through the GitHub API; omit for this checkout's GitHub repository. |  |

### Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all-repos` | Scan every repository the token can reach. |  |
| `--cache <DIR>` | Cache directory, shared across checkouts (default: `patchula` in the user cache directory: `~/Library/Caches` on macOS, else `XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache`). |  |
| `--settings <FILE>` | Operator settings file; also PATCHULA_SETTINGS (default: `patchula/settings.pkl` in `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config`, when present). |  |
| `--concurrency <N>` | Maximum concurrent repository scans (1–100), overriding the settings file; HTTP limits are per host (default: 8). |  |
| `--config <FILE>` | Local Pkl config override applied to every selected repository. |  |
| `--config-dir <DIR>` | Per-repository overrides: `DIR/<owner>/<name>.pkl`, then `DIR/<name>.pkl`; other repositories use their own `patchula.pkl`, or are skipped without one. Conflicts with `--config`. |  |
| `--dir <DIR>` | Plan branches and diffs from a local directory instead of GitHub; requires `--dry-run`. |  |
| `--recheck <WHEN>` | When a ticked PR or dashboard checkbox takes effect; also PATCHULA_RECHECK (default: next-run). One of `now`, `next-run`. |  |
| `--dry-run` | Print planned branches, files and unified diffs without writing to GitHub. |  |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples

Plan branches and diffs for acme/app, writing nothing

```sh
patchula run --dry-run acme/app
```

Open or update pull requests for acme/app

```sh
patchula run acme/app
```

Run every repository the token can reach

```sh
patchula run --all-repos --config-dir overrides
```

## `patchula serve`

- **Usage:** `patchula serve [FLAGS]`

Run the API-only GitHub App webhook server.

### Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--settings <FILE>` | Operator settings file; also PATCHULA_SETTINGS. |  |
| `--listen <ADDR>` | Server bind address; also PATCHULA_LISTEN (default: 127.0.0.1:8080). |  |
| `--cache <DIR>` | Server cache and queue directory; also PATCHULA_SERVER_CACHE (default: `patchula/server` in the user cache directory). |  |
| `--app-id <ID>` | GitHub App ID; also PATCHULA_APP_ID. |  |
| `--private-key-file <FILE>` | PEM private key file; also PATCHULA_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE. |  |
| `--webhook-secret-file <FILE>` | Webhook secret file; also PATCHULA_WEBHOOK_SECRET_FILE. |  |
| `--shutdown-timeout-secs <SECS>` | Graceful server drain deadline; also PATCHULA_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECS (default: 60). |  |
| `--recheck <WHEN>` | When a ticked PR or dashboard checkbox takes effect; also PATCHULA_RECHECK (default: now). One of `now`, `next-run`. |  |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples

Serve with operator settings

```sh
patchula serve --settings settings.pkl
```

Listen on every interface

```sh
patchula serve --settings settings.pkl --listen 0.0.0.0:8080
```

## `patchula tools`

- **Usage:** `patchula tools <SUBCOMMAND>`

Manage the lockfile runner's tool store (`PATCHULA_TOOLS_DIR`, or `tools/` in the cache directory).

### Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples

Install pinned toolchains ahead of time (e.g. in an image)

```sh
patchula tools install
```

Drop versions unused for two weeks

```sh
patchula tools prune --days 14
```

## `patchula tools prune`

- **Usage:** `patchula tools prune [--cache <DIR>] [--days <DAYS>]`

Uninstall tool versions no run has used recently; pinned defaults stay.

## `patchula tui`

- **Usage:** `patchula tui [FLAGS] [OWNER/REPO]…`

Browse dependencies and updates in the terminal; omit repositories to apply updates locally.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[OWNER/REPO]…` | Repositories as owner/repo, read through the GitHub API; omit for the current checkout. |  |

### Flags

| Flag | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all-repos` | Scan every repository the token can reach. |  |
| `--cache <DIR>` | Cache directory, shared across checkouts (default: `patchula` in the user cache directory: `~/Library/Caches` on macOS, else `XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache`). |  |
| `--settings <FILE>` | Operator settings file; also PATCHULA_SETTINGS (default: `patchula/settings.pkl` in `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config`, when present). |  |
| `--concurrency <N>` | Maximum concurrent repository scans (1–100), overriding the settings file; HTTP limits are per host (default: 8). |  |
| `--config <FILE>` | Local Pkl config override applied to every selected repository. |  |
| `--config-dir <DIR>` | Per-repository overrides: `DIR/<owner>/<name>.pkl`, then `DIR/<name>.pkl`; other repositories use their own `patchula.pkl`, or are skipped without one. Conflicts with `--config`. |  |
| `--default-config` | Use default configuration when the working tree has no `patchula.pkl`, instead of prompting. Conflicts with `--config` and `--config-dir`. |  |
| `--once` | Print a plain-text snapshot of the updates and exit with `lookup`'s exit code, for pipes and CI logs. |  |
| `-h --help` | Print help |  |

### Examples

Pick updates and apply them locally

```sh
patchula tui
```

Browse a repository through the API

```sh
patchula tui acme/app
```

Print a plain snapshot, for pipes and CI logs

```sh
patchula tui --once
```
